strings.d1.s0.name: Meidan & Sioni Katedrali
strings.d1.s0.tips: The heart of the old city: St Nino's hanging cross and Shardeni Street.
strings.d1.s1.name: Narikala Fortress Cable Car
strings.d1.s1.tips: Take the cable car from Rike Park (Metromoney card). You get a 4th-century fortress, the Mother of Georgia statue and views over the Kura.
strings.d1.s2.name: Abanotubani Sulphur Baths
strings.d1.s2.tips: Brick-domed 17th-century bathhouses where Pushkin is said to have bathed. A private room costs 50-100 GEL, scrub included. Orbeliani's facade is blue and looks like a mosque.
strings.d1.s3.name: Café Leila Old Town
strings.d1.s3.tips: Vegetarian Georgian food: try pkhali and lobio. On King Erekle Street.
strings.d1.s4.name: Bridge of Peace & Rike Park
strings.d1.s4.tips: A glass bridge lit up at night, over the Kura River.
strings.d1.b0.name: Shavi Lomi
strings.d1.b0.tips: A home-style restaurant full of art, serving modern Georgian food.
strings.d1.b1.name: Leghvtakhevi Waterfall
strings.d1.b1.tips: A waterfall behind the bath district. Free; a good alternative to a garden stroll.
strings.d2.s0.name: Rustaveli Avenue
strings.d2.s0.tips: Parliament, the Opera and the Rustaveli Theatre, in Soviet and Art Nouveau styles.
strings.d2.s1.name: Georgian National Museum
strings.d2.s1.tips: Colchis gold treasures and the Museum of Soviet Occupation, plus the Dmanisi skulls (1.8 million years old).
strings.d2.s2.name: Dry Bridge Market
strings.d2.s2.tips: A flea market selling Soviet medals, glass, kilims and paintings. Open daily, bigger at weekends.
strings.d2.s3.name: Barbarestan Khinkali
strings.d2.s3.tips: Recipes from a 19th-century cookbook. Book ahead; on Aghmashenebeli.
strings.d2.s4.name: Vino Underground Natural Wine
strings.d2.s4.tips: A bar for amber wine made in kvevri (clay vessels), an 8,000-year-old tradition. Tastings available.
strings.d2.b0.name: Fabrika Tbilisi
strings.d2.b0.tips: A hipster courtyard in a former Soviet sewing factory, with graffiti and cafes.
strings.d2.b1.name: Sofia Melnikova's Fantastic Douqan
strings.d2.b1.tips: In the garden of the Writers' House; try the khachapuri.
strings.d3.s0.name: Jvari Monastery
strings.d3.s0.tips: A 6th-century cross-shaped monastery above the meeting of the Aragvi and Kura, with Lermontov views. 30 minutes by taxi or marshrutka.
strings.d3.s1.name: Svetitskhoveli Cathedral
strings.d3.s1.tips: An 11th-century UNESCO cathedral with the legend of Christ's robe and royal tombs. Bring a headscarf.
strings.d3.s2.name: Salobie Bia Mtskheta
strings.d3.s2.tips: Lobio (bean stew) in a clay pot and mchadi cornbread: a Mtskheta classic.
strings.d3.s3.name: Samtavro Monastery
strings.d3.s3.tips: St Nino's blackberry bush and a community of nuns.
strings.d3.s4.name: Chronicle of Georgia Tbilisi
strings.d3.s4.tips: On the way back, Tsereteli's giant stone monument with views of the Tbilisi Sea.
strings.d3.b0.name: Shio-Mgvime Monastery
strings.d3.b0.tips: A 6th-century canyon monastery; an alternative to Samtavro.
strings.d3.b1.name: Chateau Mukhrani
strings.d3.b1.tips: Wine tasting and lunch in a princely chateau, 30 minutes from Mtskheta.
strings.d4.s0.name: Ananuri Fortress
strings.d4.s0.tips: On the Georgian Military Road (3 hours; tour about 80 GEL). A 17th-century fortress above the Zhinvali Reservoir.
strings.d4.s1.name: Gudauri Panorama Russia-Georgia Friendship Monument
strings.d4.s1.tips: A semicircle with Soviet mosaics at 2,400 m, with valley views and paragliding.
strings.d4.s2.name: Gergeti Trinity Church
strings.d4.s2.tips: A 14th-century church at 2,170 m facing Mount Kazbek (5,047 m). Go by 4x4 (60 GEL) or a 1.5-hour climb.
strings.d4.s3.name: Stepantsminda Lunch Khinkali
strings.d4.s4.name: Stepantsminda Kazbek View
strings.d4.s4.tips: The terrace of Rooms Hotel. The return takes 3 hours, with a stop in Pasanauri.
strings.d4.b0.name: Truso Valley
strings.d4.b0.tips: Ghost villages with mineral springs. An extra hike if you are not on a tour.
strings.d4.b1.name: Pasanauri Khinkali Stop
strings.d4.b1.tips: The town where khinkali was born; stop on the way back.
strings.d5.s0.name: Bodbe Monastery
strings.d5.s0.tips: 2 hours from Sighnaghi (tour about 100 GEL). St Nino's tomb, cypresses and the Alazani Valley.
strings.d5.s1.name: Sighnaghi
strings.d5.s1.tips: The walled "city of love" with Caucasus views, a 24-hour wedding registry and a Pirosmani museum.
strings.d5.s2.name: Pheasant's Tears Sighnaghi
strings.d5.s2.tips: Natural kvevri wines and lunch at John Wurdeman's winery. Tastings available.
strings.d5.s3.name: Kvareli Kindzmarauli Corporation
strings.d5.s3.tips: A kvevri wine producer with tastings of the semi-sweet red.
strings.d5.s4.name: Telavi & Alaverdi Monastery
strings.d5.s4.tips: Telavi's main town and the 11th-century Alaverdi Cathedral (50 m tall), then the drive back.
strings.d5.b0.name: Khareba Winery Tunnel
strings.d5.b0.tips: A 7 km wine tunnel inside the mountain, in Kvareli.
strings.d5.b1.name: Tsinandali Chavchavadze Estate
strings.d5.b1.tips: A princely manor and garden; an alternative to Telavi.
strings.d6.s0.name: Sololaki Courtyards
strings.d6.s0.tips: Art Nouveau entrances and wooden balconies, the Kalantarov house and the Betlemi stairs.
strings.d6.s1.name: Mother of Georgia Kartlis Deda
strings.d6.s1.tips: The aluminium Mother statue on Sololaki hill, holding wine and a sword.
strings.d6.s2.name: Mtatsminda Funicular & Pantheon
strings.d6.s2.tips: The funicular takes you up to 770 m. See the pantheon of Griboyedov and other writers, and St David's Church.
strings.d6.s3.name: Funicular Restaurant Mtatsminda
strings.d6.s3.tips: Lobiani and Acharuli khachapuri (boat-shaped), a city panorama and famous ponchiki.
strings.d6.s4.name: Vake Park & Turtle Lake
strings.d6.s4.tips: A park with a victory monument. Take the cable car to Turtle Lake and rent a boat.
strings.d6.b0.name: Ethnographic Museum Tbilisi
strings.d6.b0.tips: An open-air museum of Georgian houses next to Turtle Lake.
strings.d6.b1.name: Café Stamba
strings.d6.b1.tips: A stylish cafe in a Soviet printing house, in Vera.
strings.d7.theme: Dezerter Bazaar and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Dezerter Bazaar
strings.d7.s0.tips: A huge local market by the station: churchkhela, suluguni, tkemali and spices.
strings.d7.s1.name: Tsminda Sameba Cathedral
strings.d7.s1.tips: The Holy Trinity Cathedral (2004), 87 m tall with a golden dome, on Avlabari hill.
strings.d7.s2.name: Machakhela Avlabari
strings.d7.s2.tips: An Adjarian khachapuri chain; a farewell meal.
strings.d7.s3.name: Airport Bus 337 Freedom Square
strings.d7.s3.tips: Bus 337 takes 40 minutes (Metromoney), or take a Bolt for 30 GEL.
strings.d7.b0.name: Metekhi Church & Vakhtang Gorgasali
strings.d7.b0.tips: A church on a rock and a statue of the king; an alternative to the cathedral.
strings.d7.b1.name: Puri Guliani Bakery
strings.d7.b1.tips: Bread from a tone (clay oven) and lobiani, on the street.
strings.note0: A Metromoney card costs 2 GEL (metro, bus and cable car rides 1 GEL). Bolt taxis are cheap. Take airport bus 337. For Kazbegi and Kakheti, book a tour (Gamarjoba, Budget Georgia, about 80-100 GEL) or use a marshrutka.
strings.note1: Winter is 0-5°C with snow; you can ski in Gudauri, and in snow you reach Gergeti by 4x4. April-May and September-October are ideal; the Kakheti grape harvest is in October.
strings.note2: Turkish citizens enter with an ID card (1 year visa-free). Carry cash in GEL (ATMs available); cards are widely accepted. Khinkali costs 1 GEL each, khachapuri 12-18 GEL, a glass of wine 8 GEL and a bath 50-100 GEL. Tip 10%.
strings.note3: Call ahead to book a private bath room (Chreli Abano). Haggle for a Gergeti 4x4 in town. Sighnaghi is full at weekends.
strings.note4: Georgian feasts are called supra, led by a tamada (toastmaster). "Gaumarjos" means cheers. Hold khinkali by the top, sip the broth and leave the top.
strings.note5: Kvevri amber wine (UNESCO), chacha (grape brandy), churchkhela, tkemali plum sauce and pkhali.
